newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Seven says Optus settlement unlikely.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Seven says Optus settlement unlikely.

text.p: Seven Network Ltd chairman Kerry Stokes said on Wednesday it was unlikely there would be any settlement to the litigation between Seven and other Optus Vision shareholders before the court hearing scheduled for Monday.
"You will have to wait until Monday," Stokes told reporters on being asked if any settlement was likely.

Seven claims in its court action that fellow shareholders in pay television group Optus Vision had breached the Optus Vision shareholders' agreement. The ligitation is to be heard in the New South Wales Supreme Court on February 24.
Seven, a two percent shareholder in Optus Vision, has said successful litigation would mean it would be allowed to acquire Optus Vision at a discount to its full valuation.

Seven has until Thursday to decide on two offers it had to enable it to acquire all the shares in Optus Vision pending the outcome of the legal action. Seven said one of the offers is for A$648.74 million and the other is for A$533.80 million.
Seven is about 24 percent owned by its chairman Kerry Stokes and 15 percent by News Corp Ltd, which in turn jointly owns the rival Foxtel pay TV network.

Stokes told reporters after giving a speech to the Graduate School of Business Innovative Australia seminar that he would not try to merge the Optus Vision pay television service with Foxtel if he successful with the litigation.

But Stokes told the seminar there should only be one cable network in Australia. Both Optus Vision and government owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp are spending a combined A$8 billion on rolling out two cable systems to carry telephone and TV services.
"It is the coming together of the cable systems and the people that have the keys to the that are the government," Stokes told reporters.
The government is planning to sell a third of Telstra in a public share float.

Optus Vision shareholders are Optus Communications Pty Ltd and U.S. West unit Continental CableVision which both own 46.5 percent and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, which has a five percent stake.
